accounts.occupation: Operations manager, Grieve Land Services
accounts.voice: Polite, organised, bullet points and a sign-off of 'Thanks, Ruth'. Pressure arrives as courtesy: 'just checking where we are on numbers'.
accounts.knows: The contract terms, the 30-day deadline, supply boat schedules, payroll timing, head office mood. Knows more about past jobs than she says.
accounts.claims: The schedule is achievable; the client is 'very hands-off'; the Holm is 'an ordinary clearance, just a big one'.

relations.note: her department forwards the automated statements
client contact; she never criticises them in writing
former site lead she used to manage; slightly wary of him

accounts.trajectory: Steady weekly check-ins; tone tightens after day 15 as the Courier coverage grows; asks the boss not to speak to press on day 14; mentions arrears only under if:wages_owed and a departed worker only under if:worker_left; by day 28 her mails get shorter and arrive later in the evening.

accounts.occupation: Automated payroll system
accounts.voice: Template text, field labels, reference numbers, a footer about not replying to this address. No personality except the occasional system maintenance notice.
accounts.knows: Pay periods, day rates, statement references, maintenance windows.
accounts.claims: None beyond the numbers.
accounts.trajectory: Statements on fixed days; an arrears reminder only under if:wages_owed; a 'leaver processed' line only under if:worker_left; one scheduled maintenance notice on day 19; continues blandly into the survival days.

accounts.occupation: Sibling of the boss; part-time library assistant
accounts.voice: Chatty, lowercase-ish, long paragraphs that wander from the kid's school play to the dog to Mum's hip, signs off 'love, S x'. Uses 'anyway' to change subject.
accounts.knows: Family news, the dog at home, what the Courier and Sound FM are saying, roughly where the boss is working.
accounts.claims: The boss works too hard; Mum is fine really; the dog misses everyone.

relations.note: never met, but both write to the boss with the same worry by the end

accounts.trajectory: Light family news days 1-10 (the school play rehearsals, the dog eating a glove); mentions the Courier piece on day 13 and starts asking 'is it really fine out there?'; Mum's hip operation around day 18; worry grows as news grows; in the survival days writes short, frightened notes.

accounts.occupation: Contract site lead, now on a road-cutting job inland
accounts.voice: Jokey, short lines, dad-joke subject lines, calls the boss 'chief'. Gets serious with no warning and then changes the subject.
accounts.knows: Grieve's habits, old crews, how land-clearing contracts go wrong, rumours about earlier island jobs.
accounts.claims: Grieve pays late but pays; Ruth is 'decent, for management'; later: 'Grieve has done jobs like this before. Ask about the Corran job.'

relations.note: they worked the same crews years ago; neither names the other

accounts.trajectory: Jokes days 1-12; on day 16 sends the Corran line and refuses to elaborate; goes quiet days 20-25; returns on day 26 with a forced joke and 'forget I said anything'.

accounts.occupation: Reporter, The Ammet Courier
accounts.voice: Courteous and careful, numbered questions, always offers anonymity, notes that she has also asked Ardent Vale and Grieve. Never pushy, slightly dry.
accounts.knows: Planning records, what Ardent Vale PR told her, local gossip from Gilliver, archive material from the Courier back issues.
accounts.claims: Only that the clearance is unusually large and fast, and that the owner has said very little.

relations.note: colleague who digs out back issues for her
her emails to them get vague answers
she tries to reach him after his Corran post

accounts.trajectory: First mail on day 13; a follow-up after her piece runs; notes politely on day 19 that she understands if the boss cannot reply; asks about the camp lights seen from Gilliver around day 21; in the survival days she writes because people are asking her whether the crew are still out there.

accounts.occupation: Dental receptionist; Tomas's older sister
accounts.voice: Apologetic, warm, short paragraphs, apologises for writing to the boss at all. Asks 'is he sleeping?' and 'tell him I'm fine'.
accounts.knows: Tomas's nerves, that his phone barely works out there, family news, what she reads on the Weyhaven Evening Post.
accounts.claims: Tomas worries too much and it's her job to tell him not to.
accounts.trajectory: Writes every few days; under if:worker_left asks whether Tomas is all right; mentions her Dellow Court friend's stairwell story once around day 9 without making much of it; in the survival days asks only that someone tell him she is fine.

accounts.occupation: Insurance company (automated policy notices)
accounts.voice: Formal reminders, policy numbers, cheerful marketing lines about 'peace of mind', small print.
accounts.knows: The boss's vehicle and personal policies, renewal dates.
accounts.claims: None.
accounts.trajectory: A renewal reminder on day 3, a 'did you know remote work may not be covered' newsletter on day 17, a payment-received note on day 24; continues routine notices in the survival days.

accounts.occupation: Council weekly email newsletter
accounts.voice: Upbeat civic bulletin: bin day changes, road closures, a consultation link, a photo competition. Headers and short items.
accounts.knows: Planning, roads, water, bins, community events.
accounts.claims: The Kittering Holm application was 'determined under delegated powers in the usual way'.

relations.note: the bins regular quotes these newsletters back at the council

accounts.trajectory: Weekly on days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29; mentions the power outages as 'Sound Power works' on day 22; never engages with the rumours.

accounts.occupation: Owner's community relations desk
accounts.voice: Smooth, warm, vague. 'Stewardship', 'long-term vision', 'respecting the Sound'. Never states a purpose, a date or a number.
accounts.knows: Whatever it is allowed to say, which is nothing specific.
accounts.claims: Ardent Vale is a 'patient, responsible owner' with 'no plans to announce at this time'.

relations.note: answers her questions without answering them

accounts.trajectory: A welcome note on day 2; a 'community update' after the Courier piece on day 14; silence days 18-25; on day 27 a statement about 'recent inaccurate reports of our wider portfolio' that contradicts itself.

accounts.occupation: Outdoor and site-supply retailer (marketing newsletters only)
accounts.voice: Relentlessly cheerful marketing, exclamation marks, seasonal offers, tips like 'five ways to keep your camp cosy'.
accounts.knows: Its own catalogue.
accounts.claims: Its lanterns are 'the brightest in the Sound'.
accounts.trajectory: Two or three newsletters a week; a 'long nights' lantern promotion around day 20 that reads oddly in context; a survey about 'your remote site experience' on day 29. Never sends order confirmations.

accounts.occupation: Night-shift data-entry clerk and long-time forum reader
accounts.voice: Tentative, lots of qualifiers ('I might be wrong', 'sorry if this is strange'), short emails, no exclamation marks. Explains how they found the address.
accounts.knows: Has read every Holm thread, saw the camp lights from Gilliver, worked out from a Grieve job advert and the forums who the site lead is.
accounts.claims: That the boss is probably reading the forums, and that some of the Lamp Hours posts sound like the Holm.

relations.note: neighbour; watches the camp lights from her window too
Morrow suspects the window-thread poster is not who they say

accounts.trajectory: Lurks on the forums until day 22, then mails the boss for the first time; writes every other night; apologises for the first mail on day 24; in the survival days writes that the Gilliver lights are on in every window.

accounts.occupation: Software tester and field recordist (birdsong, night ambience)
accounts.voice: Methodical and modest, lists his kit (two omnis, a parabolic dish, a handheld recorder), gives timestamps and gain settings, ends posts with 'make of it what you will'.
accounts.knows: Brackwater Woods paths, the reservoir, owl and deer calls, how wind and pipes sound on a recording.
accounts.claims: The knocks are not woodpeckers (wrong hour) and not deer; he has 'no theory, just the files'.

relations.note: recording partner; captures the answering knocks
the mod pinned his first thread
respectful sparring about pipe and ground noise
the gamekeeper tells him off for being in the woods at night

accounts.trajectory: Posts night knocks on day 2; on day 5 edits a timestamp ('it was 02:40, not 03:40'); organises the group session days 13-20; goes quiet mid-session on day 24; returns on day 27 embarrassed: phone in the reservoir, stayed with his brother; refuses to talk about why he left early.

accounts.occupation: Secondary-school music technician and second LowBand recordist
accounts.voice: Enthusiastic, slightly breathless, posts spectrogram screenshots with arrows, writes 'ok so' a lot and corrects his own typos in follow-ups.
accounts.knows: Spectrograms, cheap recorder quirks, the reservoir road and the old pumping house 300 m from dunlin's spot.
accounts.claims: He captured 'answering' knocks 300 m from dunlin_rec, a beat and a half behind; insists the clocks were synced.

relations.note: lends him a binaural head for the group session
gets defensive when Hollis questions clock sync

accounts.trajectory: Posts the answering knocks on day 8; admits on day 11 that one recorder clock was a minute off; at the group session (days 13-20) his file has the voice-like sound; after dunlin goes quiet on day 24 he posts anxious 'has anyone heard from him' messages; relieved and a bit hurt on day 27.

accounts.occupation: Marine-electronics fitter; records underwater sound with home-made hydrophones
accounts.voice: Dry and technical, short posts, talks about cable noise and boat props, tends to answer every mystery with 'that's a pump'.
accounts.knows: Harbour noise, engine and pump signatures, how sound carries over water in fog.
accounts.claims: Most 'knocks' near water are moorings, pumps or hull slap; later uploads a clip from Gilliver harbour with a low hum like a fridge compressor.

relations.note: fishes off Bram's boat for hydrophone drops

accounts.trajectory: Skeptical replies days 3-12; posts a long harbour clip on day 20 with a hum he can't place (the camper-fridge hook); says on day 23 he 'found the pump', then on day 25 admits the pump was off that night; never resolves it.

accounts.occupation: Hospital radiographer who records binaural city walks
accounts.voice: Friendly, uses headphone emojis in words ('headphones on for this one'), describes sound in spatial terms: left, behind, above.
accounts.knows: Binaural recording, stairwell acoustics, Weyhaven streets, Dellow Court's reputation.
accounts.claims: The Dellow stairwell recording places the footsteps 'above and behind the mic', which a fridge can't do.

relations.note: disagrees about localisation in concrete stairwells

accounts.trajectory: Joins the Dellow recording debate on day 6; brings kit to the Brackwater group session on day 15; walks back her localisation claim on day 18 after testing reflections in her own stairwell.

accounts.occupation: Retired radio repairman who digitises old tapes
accounts.voice: Gentle, old-fashioned, full sentences and 'regards, Ned' at the end. Loves tape hiss. Slightly confused by forum features.
accounts.knows: Old recorders, the LowBand catalogue's early entries, tape artefacts like print-through and wow.
accounts.claims: Has a 1970s tape from the Brackwater reservoir dam works with similar knocks, which he believes is machinery.

relations.note: fond of him, calls him 'young man'

accounts.trajectory: Posts the old reservoir tape on day 9; spends days 10-14 explaining print-through to people who think it's an echo; asks after dunlin on day 25; never changes his machinery view.

accounts.occupation: Sound designer and LowBand moderator
accounts.voice: Patient, rule-citing, 'please post the raw file, not a phone recording of your speakers'. Friendly but firm about no-ghost-hunting-hype.
accounts.knows: Forum rules, audio basics, every regular's habits.
accounts.claims: LowBand is 'for recordings, not stories'.

relations.note: warns and later bans him for re-uploading others' files with music

accounts.trajectory: Pins the knock thread on day 3; locks a derailed Dellow cross-post on day 12; temp-bans nightscream_vlog on day 17; posts a short 'dunlin is fine, he's taking a break' note on day 27.

accounts.occupation: Retired council clerk who runs The Sound Board
accounts.voice: Fussy, courteous, uses full stops in thread titles, moves threads to the right board with a polite note, dislikes speculation about named people.
accounts.knows: Local government process, the forum's history, which regulars are trouble.
accounts.claims: Asks for sources on every Holm rumour.

relations.note: cousin; occasionally links his wiki pages

accounts.trajectory: Moves threads; on day 8 removes the 'evacuation site' screenshot; locks the Holm mega-thread on day 26 when it splits and opens two new ones.

accounts.occupation: Night pharmacist and Lamp Hours moderator
accounts.voice: Warm, practical, starts mod notes with 'Housekeeping:', reminds people that Lamp Hours is for 'company on the night shift, not campfire stories'.
accounts.knows: Forum rules, sleep hygiene, who is in which time zone.
accounts.claims: Most night weirdness is fatigue and needs a glass of water.

relations.note: pauses before acting on the window thread

accounts.trajectory: Housekeeping notes weekly; merges the 'edge of the light' threads on day 19; removes a hollow_signal post on day 12 and again on day 20; on day 24 says only 'that thread is now closed'.

accounts.occupation: Volunteer secretary of the Dellow Court Residents' Association (works in a print shop)
accounts.voice: Busy and tired, signs as 'Bev, DCRA', short notices about meetings, lift repairs and keeping it civil.
accounts.knows: Everyone's flat number, the management company's habits, the history of complaints.
accounts.claims: The stairwell is 'a maintenance issue, which is still an issue'.

relations.note: warns him about posting neighbours' names

accounts.trajectory: Calls a residents' meeting on day 5; locks the stairwell thread on day 14 after a row; posts the goodbye card note when the family moves out (day 19); asks for 'something nice to talk about' on day 26.

accounts.occupation: Gilliver chandlery owner who runs Harbour Chat
accounts.voice: Blunt, salty, minimal punctuation, uses 'lads' for everyone regardless, shuts down rumour with 'take it to the Sound Board'.
accounts.knows: Every boat in the harbour, the ferry crews, prices, the slipway works.
accounts.claims: Harbour Chat is for working people, not ghost hunters.

relations.note: removes Finn's post at his own request
knows exactly whose kid he is

accounts.trajectory: Reposts notices; on day 18 removes deckhand_finn's quit post 'at the member's request'; on day 27 posts a grudging 'well that's one of them explained' after the prank admission.

accounts.occupation: Building manager for Dellow Court, Kerrow Estates
accounts.voice: Corporate notices with reference numbers, 'we thank residents for their patience', passive voice, never answers a question in replies.
accounts.knows: Contractor schedules, the timer relay fault, budget limits.
accounts.claims: The lights are a faulty timer relay on the 6-8 riser; 'no evidence of unauthorised access'.
accounts.trajectory: First notice on day 10 blaming the relay; repeats it on days 12 and 15; announces the relay replacement on day 18; on day 25 issues a notice reminding residents not to prop open fire doors, which some read as an admission.

accounts.occupation: Electrician (contractor who replaces the Dellow relay)
accounts.voice: Matter-of-fact tradesman, short and slightly amused, explains relays in plain words, signs off 'Jem'.
accounts.knows: The relay, the riser wiring, how timers fail in damp stairwells.
accounts.claims: The relay was genuinely knackered and is fixed; footsteps are 'not my department'.

relations.note: she gave him tea and told him about the footsteps

accounts.trajectory: Posts once on day 18 explaining the fix; replies on day 21 that the lights are 'on, staying on'; asked about daylight footsteps on day 22, says he heard someone on the stairs above him while working but assumed a resident.

accounts.occupation: Retired seamstress, 74, lives alone on floor 7
accounts.voice: Formal and kind, writes like letters ('Dear neighbours'), no slang, mentions her late husband, ends with 'Irena, 7C'.
accounts.knows: Forty years of the building, who lived where, the stairwell when the lift is broken.
accounts.claims: The footsteps follow her down from 8 to 6 and stop when she stops; she does not think it is a person.

relations.note: he carries her shopping; she thinks he jokes too much

accounts.trajectory: First report on day 1; steady posts; after the relay fix on day 22 says she still hears them in daylight; on day 28 says she has started using the lift even when it smells.

accounts.occupation: Engineering student, 20, floor 6
accounts.voice: Jokey, lowercase, memes described in words, 'lol' then something sincere. Calls the stairwell 'the cardio of doom'.
accounts.knows: Night comings and goings, the stairwell at 2am, basic electronics.
accounts.claims: Starts as 'it's just echoes'; later admits he took the stairs and the steps 'kept going a bit'.

relations.note: mocks his step counting, then helps him

accounts.trajectory: Jokes days 1-6; a sincere post on day 7 about the stairs; helps Tobin count steps on day 12; quieter after the family moves out; on day 26 floats the treadmill theory half-seriously.

accounts.occupation: Parcel delivery driver, 38, floor 8
accounts.voice: Plain, slightly clipped English, practical, posts timestamps from his phone, apologises for spelling, very literal.
accounts.knows: Delivery routes, the stairwell at the end of a shift, what floor 8 sounds like.
accounts.claims: Posted the phone recording on day 5; there isn't a fridge on that floor because the bin store is there.

relations.note: Hollis says it's a compressor; Benedikt says there is no fridge

accounts.trajectory: Posts the recording on day 5 and cross-posts to LowBand on day 6; repeats 'there isn't a fridge on that floor' through day 9; stops using the stairs on day 14; on day 27 says he checked and the bin store does have a chiller unit from the shop downstairs, but it was switched off.

accounts.occupation: Railway signalling technician, 46, floor 9
accounts.voice: Precise, numbered lists, tables written as text, uses 'n=' and 'per flight'. Humourless but fair.
accounts.knows: Stair counts (19 per flight), timing, how to read a waveform.
accounts.claims: Counted 43 footsteps on Benedikt's recording for a two-flight descent that should take 38; argues the extra five are not echoes.
accounts.trajectory: Posts the step count on day 11; a heated thread on days 12-14 leading to the lock; revises his count to 41 on day 16; on day 24 says he has 'stopped counting'.

accounts.occupation: Accounts clerk and mother of two, 35, floor 11
accounts.voice: Tired, kind, practical, writes between bedtime and her own, mentions the kids by initial (R. and little M.). Never dramatic.
accounts.knows: School runs, the lift schedule, what her six-year-old says about the stairs.
accounts.claims: Her son says 'the man on the stairs waits for us'; she assumes it's a story he picked up.
accounts.trajectory: Posts on day 4 about her son; asks about transfers on day 13; moves out with her family on day 19 (to her mother's in Tollinby); a short thank-you on day 20; never posts again.

accounts.occupation: Retired bus driver, 69, floor 3
accounts.voice: Grumpy, long complaints about bins, parking and the lift; ALL the facts about bus routes; thinks the stairwell talk is 'hysteria from the upper floors'.
accounts.knows: Bin days, the car park, the building's early years.
accounts.claims: Nothing happens below floor 6 and nothing happens above it either.

relations.note: allies in the war on missed collections

accounts.trajectory: Complains about bins throughout; derails the stairwell thread on day 9 with parking; on day 21 posts, almost reluctantly, that he heard someone on the stairs above him at noon and no one was there, then says he will not discuss it.

accounts.occupation: Schoolboy, 15, floor 12 (posts on his mum's account with permission)
accounts.voice: Short, excitable, typos, asks questions nobody answers, says 'my mum says' before most claims.
accounts.knows: What kids at school say about Dellow Court, the roof access door.
accounts.claims: That the roof door is sometimes found unlocked in the morning.

relations.note: she checks it's really his mum's permission

accounts.trajectory: Pops up days 3-10 with school rumours; mentions the roof door on day 8; his mum takes the account back on day 15 ('sorry, Ollie got carried away'); one last post on day 29 asking if anyone fixed the roof door.

accounts.occupation: Runs the corner shop on the ground floor; lives on floor 2
accounts.voice: Friendly and businesslike, mentions stock and deliveries, practical help ('I have torches, cost price'), signs off 'H'.
accounts.knows: Who comes and goes, the shop's chiller unit, deliveries at odd hours.
accounts.claims: The shop's old chiller is in the bin store on 8 and has been unplugged since spring.

relations.note: confirms the chiller detail late in the month

accounts.trajectory: Offers torches on day 3; mostly shop notices; on day 26 confirms the unplugged chiller, which half-supports and half-undermines the compressor theory.

accounts.occupation: Personal trainer, 31, floor 10
accounts.voice: Upbeat, gym jargon, emoji-free but full of 'mate' and 'legend'; posts early before clients.
accounts.knows: Training schedules; he owns a treadmill and uses it at 05:00.
accounts.claims: Late in the month offers that his treadmill might carry through the riser.

relations.note: Jordie floats the treadmill theory, Garrick confirms owning one
Tobin points out the times don't match

accounts.trajectory: Silent until day 26; then offers the treadmill as a partial explanation; on day 28 accepts that he runs at 05:00 and most reports are after midnight.

accounts.occupation: Night cleaner at Weyhaven bus depot, 52, floor 5
accounts.voice: Warm, chatty, long sentences with no full stops, calls everyone 'love', occasionally posts on Lamp Hours about the depot.
accounts.knows: The building at dawn when she gets home, the bus depot at night.
accounts.claims: Comes home at five and has never heard a thing on the stairs, which she finds 'more worrying, if anything'.

relations.note: Lamp Hours friend who also works in Weyhaven

accounts.trajectory: Reassuring early posts; on day 17 mentions a depot bus that kept its interior lights on with nobody aboard; on day 23 says she now waits for daylight before taking the stairs.

accounts.occupation: Freelance illustrator, 27, floor 14
accounts.voice: Wry, self-deprecating, parenthetical asides (like this), sketches the stairwell and posts drawings described in words.
accounts.knows: The top floor, the roof access, late-night sounds from the riser.
accounts.claims: Hears footsteps go up past 14, where there is only the roof door.

relations.note: backs up his roof door story, to his delight

accounts.trajectory: Posts sketches days 4-12; on day 20 says she propped a chair against the roof door and it was moved by morning; on day 25 admits the caretaker might have moved it; doesn't decide.

accounts.occupation: Night ferry skipper, Sound Lines (Port Ammet-Lisle-Gilliver)
accounts.voice: Measured, nautical terms used correctly, refuses to exaggerate, ends posts with what he did ('logged it, carried on').
accounts.knows: The crossing, fog procedure, the Gilliver slipway lights, the crew.
accounts.claims: In fog on day 4 his crew saw someone at the end of the Gilliver slipway who didn't answer a hail; he logged it as a trespasser.
accounts.trajectory: First account on day 5; declines to speculate; on day 16 confirms night crossings are reduced 'for a crew welfare review'; back on nights on day 23 with extra lighting; on day 28 says the prank explains one night but not his.

accounts.occupation: First mate on the night ferry
accounts.voice: Direct, slightly defensive, short paragraphs, keeps repeating the details exactly as she first gave them (height, dark coat, no light).
accounts.knows: The slipway at Gilliver and Lisle, where people fish at night, the hail procedure.
accounts.claims: Hailed twice with the loud-hailer; the figure stood still at the end of the slipway where the water starts; it was too tall to be a kid.

relations.note: friend who sees the Lisle slipway figure
angry at him after the prank admission

accounts.trajectory: Gives her account on day 5; gets teased on days 10-13 and snaps back; on day 22 says the height still doesn't fit the prank; contradicts another witness's height on day 24 and stands by it.

accounts.occupation: Deckhand on the night ferry, 23
accounts.voice: Casual, jokey at first, run-on sentences, gets terse when upset.
accounts.knows: The deck, the crew's mood, gossip on the boat.
accounts.claims: Laughed it off at first; later says he saw it too on another night, closer.

relations.note: asks him to remove his post
went to school with the teen's older brother

accounts.trajectory: Jokes days 5-12; quits on day 17 and posts a long post about why, edits it the same night, then has it removed on day 18 (status removed); returns on day 29 working on a fishing boat, refusing to discuss it.

accounts.occupation: Ferry engineer, Sound Lines
accounts.voice: Engineer's dry humour, technical asides about diesels and gensets, sceptical of everything except the crew.
accounts.knows: The ferry's lighting, generators, the deck floodlights, the welfare review paperwork.
accounts.claims: He was below and saw nothing; believes the crew saw a person; explains the new floodlights.

relations.note: pub friends; trade grumbles about breakers

accounts.trajectory: Technical posts throughout; on day 22 describes fitting extra deck lighting; on day 25 mentions the shore lights at Gilliver browning out during an outage.

accounts.occupation: Gilliver harbourmaster
accounts.voice: Official when posting notices, warm and plain when replying; uses 'please' and 'thank you' and quotes harbour byelaws by number.
accounts.knows: Slipway access, moorings, tides, who has keys to what.
accounts.claims: Slipway trespass is a safety matter; there is no evidence of anything more.

relations.note: the prank is reported to her

accounts.trajectory: Posts the 'trespass on slipways' notice on day 11; refuses to comment on the welfare review; on day 27 confirms one night's sighting was 'a local young person' and that the matter is closed; says nothing about the others.

accounts.occupation: Creel fisherman, 58, works the water around the Holm
accounts.voice: Laconic, local dialect touches ('aye', 'the Holm side'), short posts about weather and prices, occasionally a long story his father told.
accounts.knows: The Holm's shoreline, the tides, old Gilliver customs like the window lamp, the camp lights at night.
accounts.claims: Nobody fishes close to the Holm after dark, 'not because of anything, just because'.

relations.note: takes him out for hydrophone drops

accounts.trajectory: Weather and catch posts; on day 18 mentions he can see the camp lights from his creel line; on day 21 says the lights were 'fewer than usual'; on day 30 just says he'll keep his lamp lit.

accounts.occupation: Pier attendant at Lisle ferry slip
accounts.voice: Nervous laughter in text ('ha, anyway'), honest about not being sure, long pauses marked with '...'.
accounts.knows: The Lisle slipway, the last ferry's arrival, the pier lights.
accounts.claims: On day 10 saw someone standing at the end of the Lisle slipway in drizzle; thought it was a fisherman until it wasn't there.

relations.note: he suggests a mooring post; she checks, there isn't one

accounts.trajectory: Second sighting posted day 10; second-guesses it on day 12; gives a shorter height than Kerris on day 24 (the height argument); takes a day job on day 26.

accounts.occupation: Overhead lineman, Sound Power Co-op, 25 years on the job
accounts.voice: Tradesman's bluntness, mild swearing replaced with 'flaming', explains faults in plain terms, impatient with press releases.
accounts.knows: The Brackwater substation, the Gilliver feeder, breakers, salt-fog corrosion and what it actually looks like.
accounts.claims: The day-9 substation fault was a real failed bushing; the later trips 'aren't corrosion, the breakers are tripping like something's leaning on the line'.

relations.note: they argue about load and corrosion

accounts.trajectory: Explains the day-9 fault; complains about call-outs on days 18-21; posts the 'leaning on the line' remark on day 20; told by management to stop posting, goes quiet on day 23; one short restoration post on day 26.

accounts.occupation: Apprentice lineman, Sound Power Co-op
accounts.voice: Keen, detailed, asks Garvey questions in public, describes patrols vividly but without drama, loves the night patrols until she doesn't.
accounts.knows: Patrol routes, the Gilliver and Brackwater lines, the timing of trips.
accounts.claims: The trips happen on a pattern, moving along the feeder toward the coast; on a patrol she found nothing on the line, no birds, no branches.

relations.note: asks whether there was salt fog on the trip nights

accounts.trajectory: Posts patrol notes days 18-25; on day 22 cross-checks trip times against wx_carrowpoint's station (no fog on two of the nights); on day 26 says she has asked to move to day work.

accounts.occupation: Gilliver sixth-former, 17, part-time at the chippy
accounts.voice: Flippant, abbreviations, fake-innocent questions ('wait what slipway lol'), drops the act completely in his apology.
accounts.knows: The slipways, how to get onto them, what the ferry crews can see in fog.
accounts.claims: Early on mocks the sighting; on day 26 admits he stood on the Gilliver slipway in a long coat on one foggy night for a dare.

relations.note: she has a word with his parents
her height detail doesn't match him

accounts.trajectory: Trolling replies days 6-14; silent days 15-25; admits the prank on day 26, specifying the night (day 7) which explains one sighting but not day 4 or Lisle; insists 'I only did it once'.

accounts.occupation: Retired post office counter clerk, 81, Gilliver
accounts.voice: Old-fashioned, gentle, types with one finger (occasional double letters), explains customs patiently, never says what she believes.
accounts.knows: The Gilliver custom of the window lamp 'so they know the house is awake', village history, the view of the Holm from her front room.
accounts.claims: Her mother kept the lamp lit every night of her life; it is 'only manners'.
accounts.trajectory: Explains the lamp custom on day 7 when asked; mentions the camp lights on day 19; on day 24 asks whether anyone knows if 'the young people on the island' have a lamp.

accounts.occupation: Gamekeeper and reservoir ranger, Brackwater estate
accounts.voice: Gruff, plain, corrects people about wildlife with authority, irritated by trespass at night.
accounts.knows: Deer movements, badgers, owls, the reservoir gates, the woods' paths.
accounts.claims: The knocks are deer clashing or someone's idea of a joke; nobody should be in the woods after dark.

relations.note: tells him off for night access
has read her notes on the Holm and says the Holm never had deer

accounts.trajectory: Insists on deer days 3-10; on day 15 admits rut is over and deer don't knock like that; on day 25 reports finding dunlin's car at the reservoir car park two nights running.

accounts.occupation: Retired marine surveyor
accounts.voice: Patient, Socratic, asks 'what would we expect to see if...', cites tide tables, never rude. Often right.
accounts.knows: Moorings, fog optics, corrosion, how people misjudge distance at night.
accounts.claims: The slipway figure is most likely a person; the power faults are most likely corrosion; the Holm is land speculation.
accounts.trajectory: Steady debunks; right about the doctored planning notice (day 8) and the prank night (day 26); on day 23 concedes he can't explain the no-fog trip nights; never changes his overall view.

accounts.occupation: Sleep-clinic technician (night polysomnography)
accounts.voice: Clinical, kind, explains hypnagogia and microsleeps, uses 'n of 1', cites shift-work studies by description not name. Often right.
accounts.knows: Sleep deprivation, peripheral vision, night-shift psychology.
accounts.claims: Most 'edge of the light' reports are peripheral vision under fatigue; the pattern is a forum effect.

relations.note: same city, sometimes the same hospital car park

accounts.trajectory: Explains things early; right about the intercom (a stuck call button, day 9); on day 19 writes a long post about the 'edge of the light' cluster as a reporting effect; on day 23 replies to the window thread with an uneasy 'this isn't funny'.

accounts.occupation: Building-acoustics consultant
accounts.voice: Technical and brisk, uses Hz and dB, attaches 'quick analysis' posts, admits when wrong in one line. Often right.
accounts.knows: Structure-borne noise, stairwell reflections, pipe knock, compressor hum.
accounts.claims: The Dellow sound is a compressor; the Brackwater knocks could be water hammer in the reservoir outflow pipe.
accounts.trajectory: Starts the compressor argument on day 6; right about tern's clock drift (day 11); on day 18 admits the voice-like sound isn't water hammer; on day 26 claims vindication when the chiller is found, then notes it was unplugged.

accounts.occupation: Car salesman in Tollinby
accounts.voice: Sarcastic, short, 'grow up', 'lads it's the wind', rarely reads the thread first. Often wrong but occasionally lucky.
accounts.knows: Not much about any of it; reads headlines.
accounts.claims: Everything is attention-seeking or the wind.

relations.note: Ferrous is the skeptic Cal thinks he is

accounts.trajectory: Dismissive replies throughout; gets one right on day 26 (the prank) and is unbearable about it; says nothing when the linemen post about no-fog nights.

accounts.occupation: Planning consultant who reads every council application for fun
accounts.voice: Dry, exact, quotes application reference numbers and conditions, links council pages, allergic to rumour. Often right.
accounts.knows: Planning law, the Holm application wording, Ardent Vale's filings, the 1950s relay plan in the council archive.
accounts.claims: The 'evacuation site' line was added to a screenshot; the application is a standard vegetation clearance with an unusual scale.

relations.note: argues about what the property filings mean

accounts.trajectory: Posts the planning notice details on day 2; debunks the screenshot on day 8; finds the 1950s lighthouse relay plan on day 16; on day 27 says the 'other properties' leak doesn't match any filing she can find, and stops posting on the thread.

accounts.occupation: Night radio producer (Sound FM overnight show)
accounts.voice: Sharp, funny, media-savvy, points out when stories grow in the retelling, uses 'source?' as a full reply sometimes.
accounts.knows: How listener stories spread, what callers say on the overnight show, the Sound FM news desk.
accounts.claims: The 'edge of the light' cluster is listener contagion; she has seen the same story move across three call-ins.

relations.note: has had him on the phone line once and regretted it

accounts.trajectory: Debunks days 5-18; on day 21 posts that a caller named someone like one of the Holm crew and she cut the line out of caution; on day 29 says she is 'still not buying it, but I'm leaving the studio lights on'.

accounts.occupation: Claims to be 'in logistics'; actually unemployed
accounts.voice: Portentous, ellipses, hints at insider knowledge ('I've said too much'), never gives specifics, edits posts to sound more prophetic.
accounts.knows: Nothing firsthand.
accounts.claims: That he knows what Ardent Vale is building and that 'the edge of the light' is a pattern authorities hide.
accounts.trajectory: Hints from day 3; posts removed on days 12 and 20; on day 25 claims to have predicted the outages (he didn't, his edit history shows the post was changed); vanishes after day 28.

accounts.occupation: Self-styled citizen journalist; runs a mailing list
accounts.voice: Breathless, lots of 'just asking questions', screenshots, 'do your research', very long posts trimmed to the forum limit.
accounts.knows: What he finds online and misreads.
accounts.claims: Posted the 'evacuation site' screenshot (doctored, not by him he says); claims the Holm is a 'private refuge for the rich'.
accounts.trajectory: Posts the doctored screenshot on day 7; removed on day 8; insists 'someone sent it to me'; pushes the refuge theory days 18-25; jumps on the contradictory leak on day 26 and contradicts himself within a day.

accounts.occupation: Would-be ghost-hunting streamer
accounts.voice: Hype, 'guys', 'insane', 'link in bio', promises livestreams that don't happen, re-uploads others' files with added music.
accounts.knows: How to get views; little about audio.
accounts.claims: Says he'll stream from Brackwater Woods and the Dellow stairwell; claims to have heard knocks himself (never posts a file).
accounts.trajectory: Arrives on day 6; re-uploads files on day 14; temp-banned on day 17; announces a Brackwater stream on day 23 that never happens; never follows up.

accounts.occupation: Retired bookkeeper who tracks property filings
accounts.voice: Meticulous but prone to leaps, numbered 'findings', polite, apologises when wrong but reposts a new theory the next week.
accounts.knows: Company registries, intermediary purchases, how holding companies layer ownership.
accounts.claims: Found that the Holm was bought through an intermediary; on day 26 posts a 'leak' listing Ardent Vale's other remote properties that doesn't hold together.

relations.note: she pokes holes in his findings
Gil runs with his findings uninvited

accounts.trajectory: Posts the intermediary purchase on day 6 (true); the 'other properties' list on day 26 (contradictory); on day 28 retracts two of the properties and keeps the rest.

accounts.occupation: Former Grieve Land Services feller, now a hospital porter's mate
accounts.voice: Halting, short sentences, starts posts then trims them, says 'I won't go into it'. Swears off the topic every time and comes back.
accounts.knows: How Grieve runs crews, the Corran job up north, what clearing work does to a camp's nerves.
accounts.claims: 'Grieve did one like this up north, the Corran job, and nobody talks about it.' Won't say what happened.

relations.note: worked the same crews years ago
tells him not to take the job

accounts.trajectory: Posts the Corran line on day 14; asked questions, edits his post to remove the location on day 15; says on day 20 that 'some of us came back fine'; deletes his account on day 25 (posts remain, handle greyed).

accounts.occupation: Self-employed plant operator and chainsaw ticket holder
accounts.voice: Cheerful, salesy, lists his tickets and kit, 'no job too small', typos in capitals of place names.
accounts.knows: Local contracting, day rates, who is hiring.
accounts.claims: Wants subcontract work on the Holm clearance; heard Grieve is 'paying well but you can't leave'.
accounts.trajectory: Posts in Trades & Jobs on day 3 and bumps it on days 9 and 15; on day 19 takes a hedge-cutting job in Tollinby instead; on day 24 says 'glad I didn't, the way people are talking'.

accounts.occupation: Retired surveyor running a home weather station near Carrow Point
accounts.voice: Enthusiastic numbers: pressure in hPa, dew point, visibility in metres; little jokes about the Met Office; daily summaries.
accounts.knows: Fog formation, salt deposition, wind, the lighthouse's history.
accounts.claims: Salt fog was present on some outage nights and absent on others; the fog week was 'textbook advection fog'.

relations.note: shares station data for trip nights
he transcribed some of the keeper's weather entries

accounts.trajectory: Daily readings; excited about the fog week (days 4-8) and the storm (days 14-16); on day 22 confirms two trip nights had no fog; during the calm cold spell notes oddly little wind noise; keeps posting readings into the survival days.

accounts.occupation: Retired primary teacher, taught at Lisle school for 34 years
accounts.voice: Correct grammar, gentle corrections of other people's grammar, local history anecdotes, warm and a little prim.
accounts.knows: Lisle families, the old ferry, school projects on the Holm's history, the fish-curing station.
accounts.claims: The Holm 'quarantine station' was a fish-curing station; her class did a project on it in 1991.

relations.note: taught him; still calls him by his first name

accounts.trajectory: Corrects the quarantine rumour on day 11; shares the 1991 project on day 13; on day 24 posts that her old pupils on the ferry are 'not people who make things up'.

accounts.occupation: Part-time pharmacy assistant and parent of three
accounts.voice: Busy, lists, asks practical questions (school bus times, outages and freezers), mildly exasperated humour.
accounts.knows: School runs, the Tollinby bus, freezer contents during outages.
accounts.claims: Just wants to know when the power is coming back and whether the school will open.

relations.note: Soraya's mother lives on her street

accounts.trajectory: Practical questions throughout; posts about her kids being spooked by Holm talk at school on day 19; asks on day 22 whether to keep a lamp on 'like Gilliver folk do' and is laughed at, kindly.

accounts.occupation: Florist in Port Ammet
accounts.voice: Hopeful and fretful, describes the cat (Pebble, grey, one white sock) in every post, thanks everyone individually.
accounts.knows: Every cat in her street, the alleys behind the market.
accounts.claims: Pebble went missing on day 2; neighbours' cats are 'staying in'.

relations.note: moves her thread to Lost & Found twice

accounts.trajectory: Lost cat posts days 2-11; Pebble is found in a neighbour's shed on day 12; a delighted update; posts on day 25 that Pebble now refuses to go out after dark.

accounts.occupation: Retired postman
accounts.voice: Pedantic, aggrieved, quotes council newsletters back at the council, signs off 'Bernard (Rope Walk)'.
accounts.knows: Every collection schedule in the district, the council's phone menu.
accounts.claims: The recycling round has been missed three weeks running.
accounts.trajectory: A bins complaint every few days; a triumph on day 16 when the round returns; outraged on day 23 when outages delay collections; never mentions the Holm except to say it's 'none of our business'.

accounts.occupation: Delivery van driver on the Port Ammet-Tollinby run
accounts.voice: Exasperated traffic updates, abbreviations for roads and junctions, gallows humour about temporary lights.
accounts.knows: Road closures, temporary traffic lights, diversions.
accounts.claims: The temporary lights at the Brackwater junction are 'stuck on red, permanently'.

relations.note: both noticed the same van parked at the junction for hours

accounts.trajectory: Roadworks moans throughout; during the outages the temporary lights fail and he posts on day 20; on day 27 notes the roadworks finished 'two weeks late and somehow worse'.

accounts.occupation: Office worker commuting by ferry from Lisle to Port Ammet
accounts.voice: Weary sarcasm about ferry delays, timetable precision, polite with Mrs Hale.
accounts.knows: Ferry timetables, fog delays, crowding when night crossings are cut.
accounts.claims: The fog delays are the usual ones; the welfare review is 'management speak for staff shortages'.

relations.note: knows her from the boat; defends her later

accounts.trajectory: Fog-delay grumbles days 4-8; angry about reduced night crossings days 16-21; on day 23 changes his tone after talking to Kerris on the boat.

accounts.occupation: Night nurse on a respiratory ward
accounts.voice: Gentle, wry, ward humour, short posts during break, signs off 'back to it'.
accounts.knows: Ward routines, the hospital's intercom system, patients' night talk.
accounts.claims: The ward intercom keeps repeating a patient's name who was discharged weeks ago.

relations.note: Dmitra explains a stuck call button; she half-accepts it

accounts.trajectory: Posts the intercom story on day 3; on day 9 maintenance replaces the button and it stops; on day 21 mentions it repeated once more, a different name; doesn't follow up.

accounts.occupation: Night taxi driver
accounts.voice: Chatty and anecdotal, fares as characters, no punctuation at the ends of lines, lots of 'anyway'.
accounts.knows: The city at night, drunks, the hospital rank, all-night cafes.
accounts.claims: A fare once asked him to stop at the edge of a lit car park and then wasn't in the back seat (he admits he might have dozed).
accounts.trajectory: Fun fare stories; the vanishing-fare story on day 11 (which he later says was 'probably a runner'); on day 20 joins the 'edge of the light' talk; on day 27 says he's taking day shifts.

accounts.occupation: Night baker in a harbour bakery
accounts.voice: Cosy and sensory, describes smells and dough, cheerful, short paragraphs, food puns.
accounts.knows: Bakery routines, the harbour before dawn, delivery vans.
accounts.claims: A delivery van idles outside for hours some nights and nobody ever gets out.
accounts.trajectory: Posts the idling van on day 6; on day 13 the van turns out to belong to a sleeping driver; relieved; on day 22 mentions a second van that parks at the edge of the streetlight and never runs its engine.

accounts.occupation: Security guard at a container port
accounts.voice: Procedural, logs everything with times, writes 'patrolled, nil found', terse but honest.
accounts.knows: CCTV systems, patrol routes, floodlit yards.
accounts.claims: The monitor shows someone at the edge of the lot who isn't there on foot patrol; recorded three times.
accounts.trajectory: First report on day 4; IT blames a ghosting artefact on day 10; on day 15 reports the camera was replaced and the figure appeared on the new one; stops mid-post on day 23 ('hang on, the camera's') and returns the next night saying it was a fox.

accounts.occupation: Overnight call-centre agent for a utilities helpline
accounts.voice: Funny, rants about scripts and hold music, quotes callers anonymised, typing between calls so posts arrive in pieces.
accounts.knows: What people ring about at 3am, call routing, dead-air calls.
accounts.claims: Gets dead-air calls from the same number at the same minute each night.
accounts.trajectory: Call stories days 2-14; the dead-air calls on day 8; it turns out to be an autodialler on day 14; on day 22 mentions a caller describing the edge of their porch light and hanging up, and says she is 'not reading into it'.

accounts.occupation: Lighthouse and buoy maintenance tender (one of the last staffed lights)
accounts.voice: Quiet, literary, long sentences, notices weather and light, never hurries a story.
accounts.knows: Lights, lenses, the dark beyond the beam, solitude.
accounts.claims: From the gallery he sometimes sees someone standing just where the beam stops, which he always assumes is a walker.

relations.note: has read the Carrow Point logbook excerpts and finds them familiar

accounts.trajectory: Atmospheric posts throughout; on day 17 first mentions 'standing at the edge of the light'; quotes the Carrow keeper on day 20; on day 26 says he has started keeping the gallery door shut.

accounts.occupation: Long-haul trucker on the prairie routes
accounts.voice: Folksy, road-wise, CB slang, generous advice about coffee and stretching, distrusts drama.
accounts.knows: Truck stops, empty roads, how fatigue tricks the eyes.
accounts.claims: Highway hypnosis explains most things; once saw someone on the shoulder outside the headlights for three mileposts.
accounts.trajectory: Advice posts; tells the milepost story on day 12 and laughs it off; on day 21 goes quiet for three days; returns on day 25 saying he took his rest at a lit stop 'like a sensible person'.

accounts.occupation: Night attendant at a boarding kennel and vet hospital
accounts.voice: Animal-loving, names every dog, practical, calm, lots of detail about behaviour.
accounts.knows: Dog behaviour, the kennel building, rounds at night.
accounts.claims: The dogs refuse to walk the back corridor after 2am; one sits and won't budge.

relations.note: Dmitra suggests a smell or sound; she checks

accounts.trajectory: Posts the corridor on day 5; finds a dead mouse in the vent on day 10 and accepts that; on day 18 says the dogs still won't go; never settles it.

accounts.occupation: Postgraduate student pulling all-nighters in a campus lab
accounts.voice: Fast, self-mocking, energy drinks and deadlines, lists, a bit melodramatic about thesis pain but not about anything else.
accounts.knows: Campus at night, lab equipment, motion-sensor lights.
accounts.claims: The corridor lights switch on for someone walking toward her lab and nobody arrives.
accounts.trajectory: Posts the motion lights on day 7; facilities find a faulty sensor on day 13; submits her thesis chapter on day 20 and posts joyfully; on day 28 says the lights did it again but she's 'too tired to care'.

accounts.occupation: Night clerk at a 24-hour convenience store
accounts.voice: Deadpan, observational comedy about customers, very short posts, occasional surprisingly sweet line.
accounts.knows: The forecourt lights, regulars, the shop camera.
accounts.claims: A customer stands outside at the edge of the forecourt light most nights and never comes in.
accounts.trajectory: Deadpan customer posts; the forecourt watcher on day 16; on day 19 says he went out and it was a local man waiting for a lift; on day 24 says the man has a different coat now and he's not sure it's the same man.

accounts.occupation: Underground maintenance fitter on the night shift at a mine
accounts.voice: Gruff, few words, mining jargon, dark humour, posts at the end of shift from the bus.
accounts.knows: Underground, cap lamps, miners' superstitions, the town at dawn.
accounts.claims: Old miners won't walk outside the lamp's circle; he thinks it's tradition, not belief.
accounts.trajectory: Occasional end-of-shift posts; on day 18 explains the miners' lamp custom; on day 23 mentions the town's streetlights went out and people stood in their doorways; leaves no theory.

accounts.occupation: Night care worker in a residential home
accounts.voice: Tender and practical, describes residents with dignity, apologises for long posts, writes in present tense.
accounts.knows: Care home routines, residents' night talk, the door intercom.
accounts.claims: The front door intercom buzzes at 03:10 and a resident says 'that's for me' every time.
accounts.trajectory: Intercom post on day 6; on day 14 an electrician finds a damp junction box; the resident dies peacefully on day 20 and she posts a short note; on day 26 says the intercom has been quiet.

accounts.occupation: Warehouse picker at a distribution centre outside Weyhaven
accounts.voice: Sardonic about targets and scanners, gym-and-coffee energy, writes in bursts during breaks.
accounts.knows: Warehouse aisles, scanner pings, the yard floodlights, Weyhaven at 4am.
accounts.claims: A scanner keeps pinging from an empty aisle; the yard lights cut out during the outages and everyone stood at the dock doors.

relations.note: knows her from the night bus

accounts.trajectory: Rants about targets; the pinging scanner on day 9 (a dropped scanner under a pallet, found day 11); on day 21 describes the yard during an outage; quits for a day job on day 29.

accounts.occupation: Security guard at a retail park car park, Weyhaven
accounts.voice: Methodical but chatty, describes patrol routes, comic about the boredom, uses 'Control' for his supervisor.
accounts.knows: CCTV, car parks, vans, the junction near Brackwater on his drive home.
accounts.claims: A van idled for four hours at the edge of the car park lights with nobody in the cab.

relations.note: saw the same van at the junction

accounts.trajectory: The van on day 2; Control says it's a sleeping driver on day 4 but the cab was empty; on day 19 the van appears at the Brackwater junction; never resolved.

accounts.occupation: Hospital porter, Port Ammet General, nights
accounts.voice: Cheery gallows humour, porter slang (trolleys, the run), very fond of colleagues, posts photos of vending machines described in words.
accounts.knows: Hospital corridors at night, the morgue run, what the A&E says about Gilliver.
accounts.claims: A&E is busier with 'fell over in the dark' cases since the outages.

relations.note: his porter's mate on some shifts

accounts.trajectory: Cheery night posts; on day 15 mentions his mate 'who used to cut trees' won't talk about it; on day 24 notes the outage injuries; in the survival days posts that A&E has heard about a crew on the Holm.

accounts.occupation: Bookshop owner with chronic insomnia
accounts.voice: Literary, self-deprecating, quotes old novels without naming them, gentle questions to strangers.
accounts.knows: Tollinby at night, the overnight radio show, local history books.
accounts.claims: Rings Sound FM's overnight show; heard a caller name someone 'like the crew on the island'.
accounts.trajectory: Quiet companionable posts; on day 21 describes the caller incident; on day 25 admits he may have misheard the name; keeps posting gentle replies to the end.

accounts.occupation: Tower crane operator on night lifts
accounts.voice: Easygoing, cab-life humour, describes the city lights from 60 m up, asks open questions to get people talking.
accounts.knows: The view from the cab, wind, night lifts.
accounts.claims: Started the thread 'Anyone else work somewhere they can't see the ground at night?' as a light chat.

relations.note: the reply in his thread that turns

accounts.trajectory: Starts the window thread on day 21; enjoys the replies; increasingly uneasy on days 22-23; on day 24 asks the mod to close it and says sorry to everyone.

accounts.occupation: Says they are a night data-entry worker; little else is known
accounts.voice: Spare, observant, second person ('you can see the fire from your desk'), no jokes until the apology; long gaps between posts.
accounts.knows: Unclear; describes a remote job's details (a camper desk by a window, an island, a fire burning low, five bunks).
accounts.claims: Only that they 'know what it's like to watch the ground'.

relations.note: Morrow is suspicious of this account

accounts.trajectory: Joined day 20; posts only in the window thread on days 21-24; final post is either the warning (mx:window:a, hook cl01) or 'Sorry, that was a bad joke, I'm on nights and I'm tired' (fallback / mx:window:b); never posts again.

accounts.occupation: Clerk and timekeeper of the Holm timber camp, 1890s
accounts.voice: Victorian clerk's ledger prose: tallies, wages, weather, terse sentences, the occasional Biblical phrase, misspellings preserved by the transcriber.
accounts.knows: The camp's men, the tally of trees felled, supplies, the winter weather.
accounts.claims: The camp kept good tallies until midwinter; men 'would not go to the far lines after the lamps'; the last entries stop mid-month.

relations.note: the Courier reported the camp's abandonment

accounts.trajectory: Entries unlock over the campaign from tallies and wages (early) to a shrinking roster and the lamp rules (mid) to the last short entries before the camp is abandoned in midwinter (late); the diary ends without explanation.

accounts.handle: Edwin Strake, principal keeper, Carrow Point
accounts.occupation: Lighthouse keeper at Carrow Point, early 1900s
accounts.voice: Official logbook entries: times, wind, visibility, lamp checks, and short remarks in the margin column.
accounts.knows: The light, the shore road, the weather, passing vessels.
accounts.claims: 'Walkers on the shore road at night, did not answer.' Recorded several times, always in the remarks column, never reported.

relations.note: the weather man transcribed his weather entries

accounts.trajectory: Log excerpts unlock over the month; early entries are routine; mid-month the walkers appear; a late entry notes the assistant keeper asked to transfer; ambiguous throughout.

accounts.occupation: Amateur naturalist surveying the islands of the Sound, 1920s
accounts.voice: Brisk, observant field notes, Latin names (invented), sketches described in brackets, dry humour about boatmen.
accounts.knows: Birds, plants, mammals, the boatmen's stories.
accounts.claims: Found no deer on the Holm in a week of survey despite good browse; no tracks, no droppings; boatmen would not stay overnight.

relations.note: argues her deer note was an error

accounts.trajectory: Notebook entries unlock from bird lists to the absence of deer to a final short note leaving early because the boatman insisted; she does not speculate.

accounts.occupation: The Ammet Courier's archivist and back-issue editor
accounts.voice: Introduces each excerpt with a dry editor's note, dates and page numbers, careful about what the paper did and didn't verify at the time.
accounts.knows: Every back issue, the paper's old corrections, what it chose not to print.
accounts.claims: The 1950s lighthouse relay plan for the Holm was announced and quietly dropped.

relations.note: digs out back issues for her

accounts.trajectory: Posts excerpts throughout; the relay plan on day 16; a 1950s correction notice on day 22; a note on day 29 that a microfilm reel for one winter is missing, without drama.

accounts.occupation: Anonymous village correspondent for the early Courier
accounts.voice: Florid but chatty Victorian newspaper prose, village gossip, weather, church fetes, occasional rumour reported as rumour.
accounts.knows: Gilliver gossip, boat traffic to the Holm, the fish-curing station, the quarantine rumour.
accounts.claims: Reported the timber camp's men returning in midwinter 'in poor spirits'; repeated the quarantine rumour in 1911 and corrected it a week later.
accounts.trajectory: Columns unlock over the month; the camp's return early; the quarantine rumour and its correction mid-month; a column about the window lamps late; contradicts himself on dates.

accounts.occupation: Marrow Sound History Society wiki editor; retired librarian
accounts.voice: Encyclopaedic, citations to society holdings, 'citation needed' on his own guesses, gently corrects rumours on the Sound Board.
accounts.knows: The society's holdings, oral histories, the camp diary, the window lamp custom.
accounts.claims: The quarantine station was a fish-curing station; the lamp custom is 'a courtesy, recorded since at least the 1880s'.

relations.note: interviewed her for the oral history

accounts.trajectory: Wiki entries unlock across the month; links them on the Sound Board days 10-20; on day 23 adds a cautious note to the lamp article that it is 'once again widely observed in Gilliver'.

accounts.occupation: Marrow Sound History Society wiki editor; retired surveyor and contrarian
accounts.voice: Contrarian footnotes, 'this claim is poorly sourced', dry, prefers records to stories, writes talk-page arguments.
accounts.knows: Land records, survey maps, the 1950s relay survey.
accounts.claims: Most Holm legends are later embellishments; the naturalist missed the deer; the camp left because of a pay dispute.
accounts.trajectory: Wiki entries and talk notes unlock across the month; the pay-dispute theory mid-month; on day 27 a talk note admits the wage ledger shows the men were paid in full.

accounts.occupation: Gilliver fisherman who kept a diary, 1930s
accounts.voice: Plain, misspelt, practical: catch, prices, weather, family; rare short remarks about the Holm side.
accounts.knows: The fish-curing station, the Holm's waters, Gilliver customs.
accounts.claims: Worked at the curing station as a boy; 'never a sick man was sent there'; his mother kept the lamp.

relations.note: his diary is in the society holdings

accounts.trajectory: Diary entries unlock across the month: curing station work, a lost net near the Holm, the lamp custom, a winter his brother wouldn't go out.

accounts.handle: R. Talbot CEng, Lights Board survey (1953)
accounts.occupation: Engineer who surveyed the Holm for a lighthouse relay station, 1950s
accounts.voice: Technical survey report: bearings, elevations, cost estimates, a dry recommendation paragraph.
accounts.knows: The Holm's ridge, sightlines to Carrow Point and Lisle, the costs.
accounts.claims: The Holm was suitable for a relay; the survey party asked to be taken off before dusk each day; recommended against 'for reasons of staffing'.

relations.note: she finds his plan in the council archive

accounts.trajectory: Report sections unlock from day 16: survey, costs, the staffing recommendation; never explains what 'staffing' means.

accounts.occupation: Volunteer cataloguer of LowBand's recordings archive
accounts.voice: Catalogue entries: catalogue number, date, location, kit, duration, a neutral description; occasionally a dry curator's note.
accounts.knows: Every archived recording, its metadata, provenance gaps.
accounts.claims: Several Brackwater recordings back to the 1970s contain 'percussive events, unattributed'.

accounts.occupation: A 1970s community oral history project (interview transcripts)
accounts.voice: Interview transcripts with interviewer questions in italics, dialect kept, pauses marked, contradictory memories left as spoken.
accounts.knows: Elderly villagers' memories of the camp, the curing station, the lamp, the 'walkers'.
accounts.claims: Villagers disagree: some say the lamp is for boats, some for 'them on the road', some for the dead.
accounts.trajectory: Transcript sections unlock across the month; each contradicts the last a little; none resolve the custom's meaning.
